subject.title: RFC: Skill routing metadata and evaluation hints for Harness-style OpenClaw setups

question: Which minimal metadata, if any, should ClawHub standardize first, and must every field remain publisher-supplied advisory data rather than a routing, permission, or security decision?
rationale: The source has an established optional metadata framework, but selecting field scope and the trust semantics determines public API compatibility and security expectations; this cannot be safely inferred from the RFC alone.

options.title: Adopt a narrow advisory v1
options.body: Standardize bounded intents/keywords plus verification descriptions, expose raw values only, and explicitly exclude risk enforcement, ranking guarantees, and runtime permission effects.

options.title: Include advisory risk hints
options.body: Add a limited risk/preflight vocabulary only if it is clearly presented as untrusted publisher disclosure alongside—not instead of—ClawHub scanner and moderation evidence.

options.title: Defer registry metadata
options.body: Keep existing semantic/vector discovery and revisit after a concrete Harness consumer proves which fields improve selection without creating a misleading trust signal.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow advisory v1
recommendation.body: Standardize bounded intents/keywords plus verification descriptions, expose raw values only, and explicitly exclude risk enforcement, ranking guarantees, and runtime permission effects.

likelyOwner.reason: The current vision and product-boundary history places the registry-versus-runtime and trust-presentation decision closest to this owner.
